accepted: Accepted as written by the owner on 28 Oct 2026 (Module 04 review, R7.4; docs/25 §9): CanDo's published starting framework, which each organization copies and edits.
source: Provided by the owner (Unified Competency Model with Behavioral Examples, October 2026). Core and Leadership indicators as provided; Functional indicators proposed in docs/19 §3.5 and accepted by the owner.

scale.descriptor_en: Applies the competency in routine, well-defined situations with guidance. Influence: own tasks.
scale.descriptor_fr: Applique la compétence dans des situations courantes et bien définies, avec encadrement. Influence : ses propres tâches.

scale.descriptor_en: Applies the competency independently in typical situations and adapts it to the person or situation. Influence: own work and clients.
scale.descriptor_fr: Applique la compétence de façon autonome dans des situations habituelles et l’adapte à la personne ou à la situation. Influence : son travail et sa clientèle.

scale.descriptor_en: Applies the competency in complex or unfamiliar situations and coaches others. Influence: the team.
scale.descriptor_fr: Applique la compétence dans des situations complexes ou nouvelles et accompagne les autres. Influence : l’équipe.

scale.descriptor_en: Shapes how the competency is practised across a program, function or department, through standards, systems and partnerships. Influence: the unit and its partners.
scale.descriptor_fr: Façonne la pratique de la compétence dans un programme, une fonction ou un service, au moyen de normes, de systèmes et de partenariats. Influence : l’unité et ses partenaires.

scale.descriptor_en: Sets direction for the competency across the organization or the wider system. Influence: the organization, funders and community.
scale.descriptor_fr: Oriente la compétence à l’échelle de l’organisation ou du système. Influence : l’organisation, les bailleurs de fonds et la communauté.

competencies.definition_en: Upholds and models integrity, equity, inclusion, and respect for people.

indicators_en: Acknowledges organizational values and codes of conduct.
Follows basic confidentiality rules in day-to-day tasks.
Avoids participating in workplace gossip.
Asks questions when unsure about the ethical course of action.
Recognizes and respects diversity in personal interactions.
Consistently demonstrates honesty in communications.
Reports minor ethical concerns to the appropriate supervisor.
Fulfills obligations even when unsupervised.
Maintains neutrality in political or cultural discussions at work.
Stays transparent about workload capacity and commitments.
Speaks up against discriminatory remarks or behavior.
Escalates ethical issues even when doing so is unpopular.
Mentors others on proper conduct in challenging situations.
Ensures fair treatment of all team members in delegating work.
Models equitable behavior during service delivery.
Leads discussions about equity and ethics during team meetings.
Creates tools or resources to help others understand ethics policies.
Intervenes constructively when witnessing workplace bias.
Promotes a speak-up culture without fear of retaliation.
Assesses and corrects fairness issues in HR or hiring processes.
Champions the integration of equity in strategic planning.
Leads initiatives that address systemic ethical concerns.
Advises senior leadership on embedding ethics into policies.
Creates an internal ethics committee or system for peer review.
Implements training programs on unconscious bias and integrity.

competencies.definition_en: Consistently seeks to understand and meet the needs of clients from diverse backgrounds.

indicators_en: Greets clients warmly and listens when they speak.
Provides basic information to clients upon request.
Refers clients to others when unsure about their needs.
Avoids making assumptions about client backgrounds.
Checks in to ensure basic satisfaction after service.
Clarifies client needs using simple questioning.
Follows up to ensure referrals were received.
Adapts approach for clients with language barriers.
Maintains respect and confidentiality with clients.
Uses checklists or forms to ensure all needs are assessed.
Creates individualized service plans based on assessment.
Advocates for client needs within and beyond the organization.
Balances empathy with professional boundaries.
Collaborates with other service providers to support the client.
Adjusts services based on evolving client situations.
Leads initiatives to improve client experience organization-wide.
Coaches colleagues on client-centered practices.
Develops feedback loops to gather client input regularly.
Customizes resources to reflect cultural and demographic needs.
Proactively resolves complex client service challenges.
Designs service models rooted in co-creation with clients.
Establishes partnerships to address systemic service gaps.
Implements organization-wide standards for inclusive service.
Leads advocacy campaigns based on client experience data.
Influences sector policy to enhance client-centered frameworks.

competencies.definition_en: Communicates effectively and works constructively with others to achieve results.

indicators_en: Responds politely to emails and phone calls.
Participates in team discussions when prompted.
Uses basic tools to share information with others.
Clarifies own understanding when confused.
Keeps others informed of availability and task status.
Explains ideas clearly and listens to feedback.
Asks for help when needed to complete group tasks.
Uses culturally sensitive language in conversations.
Works respectfully with others from diverse backgrounds.
Offers suggestions during group meetings.
Leads small group discussions to solve problems.
Gives and receives constructive feedback regularly.
Tailors communication to different audiences.
Facilitates consensus during decision-making.
Supports colleagues during high-pressure periods.
Mediates conflicts between team members.
Designs communication strategies for difficult topics.
Builds collaboration with external partners.
Mentors others on professional communication.
Encourages cross-functional knowledge sharing.
Establishes strategic communication frameworks.
Advises executives on sensitive communication issues.
Champions organization-wide collaboration norms.
Develops inclusive language guidelines for the organization.
Leads cross-sector communication initiatives.

competencies.definition_en: Adjusts to change, learns continuously, and supports a culture of growth and innovation.

indicators_en: Responds calmly to minor changes in schedule.
Accepts new tools or processes after some explanation.
Adjusts workflow slightly when required by supervisor.
Attends required training sessions without complaint.
Seeks help when facing new tasks.
Volunteers for small changes in team assignments.
Learns from experience and applies it to future tasks.
Asks questions to improve understanding of new systems.
Adapts communication style to different team members.
Implements feedback received from supervisors.
Quickly integrates new policies or procedures into daily work.
Improves outdated practices with innovative suggestions.
Self-initiates learning on new tools or trends.
Shares learning tips with peers after training.
Adjusts service delivery for remote or hybrid environments.
Coaches team members through transitions and change.
Creates learning plans tailored to team or project needs.
Models growth mindset in response to setbacks.
Leads debrief sessions to capture lessons learned.
Adapts workflows quickly in crisis or ambiguity.
Drives organizational agility through strategy and process.
Champions continuous improvement initiatives.
Builds a learning culture that supports experimentation.
Identifies long-term learning trends for strategic planning.
Establishes cross-training programs across departments.

competencies.definition_en: Focuses on achieving high-quality outcomes and improving performance.

indicators_en: Completes assigned tasks on time with supervision.
Double-checks work for basic accuracy.
Asks for clarification when unclear about goals.
Meets minimum standards for quality.
Communicates delays when they arise.
Sets daily or weekly goals to manage time effectively.
Takes ownership of assigned tasks from start to finish.
Suggests small improvements to processes.
Regularly tracks progress toward deliverables.
Adjusts pace to meet tight deadlines when needed.
Identifies barriers to results and addresses them.
Improves efficiency of recurring work tasks.
Leads a small project to completion within scope.
Uses performance data to improve quality.
Mentors peers on effective goal setting.
Drives high performance through coaching and structure.
Sets ambitious but achievable targets for programs.
Optimizes cross-functional workflows for better outcomes.
Aligns team activities with strategic goals.
Holds others accountable with support and feedback.
Champions a results-driven culture across the organization.
Integrates performance data into decision-making processes.
Designs systems to track and report key success metrics.
Drives innovation to improve service outcomes.
Aligns strategic planning with measurable results.

competencies.definition_en: Leads, motivates, and develops individuals and teams to deliver results.

indicators_en: Shares clear instructions and basic expectations with team members.
Participates in team check-ins without directing others.
Supports peer collaboration without formal leadership role.
Offers to coordinate small group efforts when asked.
Recognizes others' contributions informally.
Delegates tasks based on individual strengths.
Monitors team progress and provides encouragement.
Addresses minor team issues with guidance from a supervisor.
Clarifies team roles and responsibilities.
Encourages mutual respect among team members.
Sets team goals and aligns individual work accordingly.
Facilitates team problem-solving sessions.
Resolves interpersonal conflicts diplomatically.
Recognizes high performance and provides constructive feedback.
Mentors junior team members to build capability.
Drives team accountability and fosters collaboration.
Builds a strong, inclusive team culture.
Coaches team members for career growth.
Leads cross-functional initiatives to drive impact.
Anticipates and addresses team capacity issues proactively.
Develops long-term talent strategies for the organization.
Builds high-performance teams aligned to strategic goals.
Models distributed leadership and empowerment.
Establishes systems to measure team effectiveness and engagement.
Leads organizational culture and values through leadership behavior.

competencies.definition_en: Aligns daily work to long-term organizational objectives and future trends.

indicators_en: Understands and supports team’s overall mission.
Focuses on immediate tasks without losing sight of big picture.
Follows direction on new strategic initiatives.
Connects own work to team goals.
Expresses curiosity about organization’s long-term plans.
Identifies how short-term tasks align with long-term goals.
Suggests improvements based on client or team feedback.
Analyzes patterns in service delivery.
Participates in planning meetings with constructive input.
Balances daily responsibilities with future impact in mind.
Contributes to operational planning aligned with strategy.
Uses data to shape program or team objectives.
Anticipates client or community needs based on trends.
Aligns team activities to strategic priorities.
Links decisions to long-term value and sustainability.
Leads strategic planning sessions.
Translates vision into actionable team goals.
Forecasts trends and prepares scenarios.
Aligns resources with changing priorities.
Integrates insights from multiple functions into planning.
Develops and communicates a compelling vision for the future.
Shapes long-term strategy through policy and partnerships.
Influences sector-wide strategic direction.
Creates a culture of strategic alignment across teams.
Evaluates risk and opportunity across multiple time horizons.

competencies.definition_en: Drives and manages change initiatives while supporting others through transitions.

indicators_en: Accepts new procedures or technologies with guidance.
Expresses openness to change even if uncertain.
Asks questions to understand reasons for changes.
Supports colleagues who are struggling with change.
Shares feedback about how change affects daily work.
Explains the purpose of changes to others in plain language.
Adjusts own work processes in response to change.
Keeps a positive tone when discussing change.
Provides examples of how change has led to improvements.
Encourages peers to try new approaches.
Coordinates implementation of a new process within the team.
Gathers and responds to feedback during transitions.
Models flexible behavior under pressure.
Coaches others on adapting to new systems or tools.
Aligns project goals with organizational change plans.
Leads planning and communication for major change initiatives.
Creates action plans to address change resistance.
Designs feedback loops during rollout phases.
Engages key stakeholders in co-creating the change process.
Builds morale and clarity during uncertainty.
Develops organization-wide change strategies.
Leads culture change aligned to vision and values.
Champions adaptive leadership across teams.
Uses change management frameworks (e.g., ADKAR, Kotter).
Advises executives and boards on transformation readiness.

competencies.definition_en: Understands, respects, and adapts services to different cultural, linguistic, and social perspectives.
competencies.note: The workbook repeats the same five examples at every level. They are kept as original_examples (they read as level 2 practice); the progression below was proposed in docs/19 §3.5 and accepted by the owner on 28 Oct 2026.
original_examples: Seeks translation support to improve client experience.
Learns about clients’ cultural norms before conducting an interview.
Modifies program delivery to accommodate cultural holidays.
Responds respectfully to religious accommodation requests.
Participates in cultural safety training and shares learnings with peers.

indicators_en: Uses respectful, plain language and checks that clients from different backgrounds have understood.
Asks clients how they prefer to be addressed and which language they prefer to use.
Requests an interpreter when a client needs one, following the program's procedure.
Learns about the communities the program serves through orientation and training.
Notices cultural needs that procedures do not cover and asks a supervisor how to respond.
Learns about a client's cultural norms before an interview and adjusts the approach.
Arranges interpretation or translated materials without being asked.
Adjusts scheduling and program delivery for cultural and religious observances.
Responds respectfully to religious and cultural accommodation requests.
Takes part in cultural safety training and shares what was learned with peers.
Adapts assessments and service plans to a client's cultural, linguistic and family context.
Recognizes when a policy or practice creates a barrier for a community and proposes a change.
Builds working relationships with cultural and community organizations to improve referrals.
Coaches colleagues on culturally safe practice in difficult situations.
Brings cultural and language considerations into case reviews and program feedback.
Designs or revises programs with input from the communities they serve.
Leads culturally safe and trauma-informed practice across a team or program.
Analyses service data by language or community to find gaps in access and outcomes.
Develops partnerships that bring community leaders and knowledge keepers into program design.
Builds cultural safety into staff orientation, supervision and quality reviews.
Sets organization-wide commitments and measures for cultural safety and inclusion.
Embeds reconciliation and anti-racism principles in strategy, policy and governance.
Represents the organization with funders, governments and communities on culturally responsive service.
Ensures interpretation, translation and community liaison resources are funded and sustained.
Holds leaders accountable for culturally responsive outcomes.

competencies.definition_en: Identifies client needs and connects them to relevant supports, services, or systems.
competencies.note: The workbook repeats the same five examples at every level. They are kept as original_examples (they read as level 2 practice); the progression below was proposed in docs/19 §3.5 and accepted by the owner on 28 Oct 2026.
original_examples: Uses a structured intake form to uncover hidden client needs.
Links newcomer families to food security programs proactively.
Assists a client in applying for income support based on their unique needs.
Explains government benefits in a culturally appropriate way.
Refers a youth to a mentorship program based on career goals.

indicators_en: Completes the standard intake accurately and on time.
Gives clients accurate information about the program's services and eligibility.
Refers clients to services from an established resource list.
Recognizes urgent safety concerns and escalates them right away.
Records referrals and follow-ups in the client file.
Uses a structured intake to uncover needs a client may not mention at first.
Links clients and families to community programs, such as food security or income support, based on their needs.
Helps clients apply for benefits and programs, explaining them in plain, culturally appropriate language.
Matches referrals to the client's own goals, such as a youth's career interests.
Follows up to confirm that the client was connected and the referral helped.
Assesses complex situations with several needs and sets priorities with the client.
Guides clients through several systems at once, such as housing, health, income and legal services.
Advocates with other agencies when a client is wrongly refused a service.
Uses assessment tools consistently and explains the findings to the team.
Coaches newer staff on intake and referral practice.
Designs or selects assessment tools and referral pathways for a program.
Builds referral agreements with partner agencies and monitors how well they work.
Reviews assessment quality across the team and acts on gaps.
Uses needs data to identify service gaps and propose new services.
Leads case conferences for the most complex situations.
Sets the organization's approach to assessment, navigation and coordinated access.
Shapes referral networks across the system with funders and partners.
Uses community needs data to guide strategy and funding requests.
Represents the organization at system planning tables.
Ensures navigation services are evaluated for outcomes and equity.

competencies.definition_en: Develops and executes structured plans to support clients or projects effectively.
competencies.note: The workbook repeats the same five examples at every level. They are kept as original_examples (they read as level 2 practice); the progression below was proposed in docs/19 §3.5 and accepted by the owner on 28 Oct 2026.
original_examples: Creates a multi-step action plan aligned with client goals.
Coordinates with housing providers to align client move-in timelines.
Follows up with partner organizations to ensure service delivery.
Adjusts service timelines when new barriers emerge.
Uses a project management tool to track tasks across partners.

indicators_en: Follows each client's service plan and completes assigned tasks on time.
Keeps client files and schedules up to date.
Tells a supervisor when a plan is not working or a deadline is at risk.
Coordinates appointments and logistics for clients.
Prepares materials for program sessions.
Develops service plans with clients, with clear goals, steps and dates.
Coordinates with the other staff and agencies involved in a client's plan.
Reviews progress with the client and adjusts the plan.
Organizes program sessions or small events from start to finish.
Documents outcomes against the plan's goals.
Plans and coordinates services for clients with complex, multi-agency plans.
Manages a caseload or small project, balancing priorities and deadlines.
Leads case conferences and coordinates partners' roles.
Identifies risks in a plan and puts mitigation in place.
Improves planning templates or workflows for the team.
Plans and manages a program or major project, including budget, staffing and timelines.
Sets service standards and monitors caseloads and outcomes.
Coordinates several teams or partner agencies toward shared goals.
Reports progress and outcomes to funders.
Adjusts program plans based on evaluation results.
Sets multi-year service plans aligned with strategy and funding.
Coordinates services across programs and sites.
Secures and allocates resources for service delivery.
Establishes the organization's evaluation and outcome framework.
Leads system-level planning with funders and partners.

competencies.definition_en: Uses technology to deliver services, document interactions, and manage data ethically.
competencies.note: The workbook repeats the same five examples at every level. They are kept as original_examples (they read as level 2 practice); the progression below was proposed in docs/19 §3.5 and accepted by the owner on 28 Oct 2026.
original_examples: Uses digital tools to create accessible service documents.
Teaches clients how to use online portals for immigration updates.
Logs case notes accurately into a centralized CRM system.
Troubleshoots tech issues for a remote client consultation.
Supports staff by developing a how-to guide for a new database.

indicators_en: Uses the organization's core systems, such as email, calendar and the client database, for daily work.
Records case notes accurately and on time in the client system.
Follows privacy and security rules for client information, including passwords and screen locks.
Asks for help when a system or tool is unfamiliar.
Recognizes and reports suspicious emails and links.
Creates accessible documents and digital materials for clients.
Helps clients use online portals and services, such as government or immigration portals.
Supports remote consultations and solves common technical issues.
Uses reports from the client system to track own caseload.
Protects personal information when sharing documents and messages.
Writes how-to guides and trains colleagues on a new system or tool.
Uses data from the client system to spot trends in own program.
Improves digital forms or workflows to save time or reduce errors.
Advises the team on privacy-safe ways to use technology with clients.
Tests new tools and gives structured feedback before roll-out.
Leads the adoption of a system or digital service for a program or department.
Defines data quality standards and checks that the team meets them.
Builds reports and dashboards that inform program decisions.
Assesses the privacy and security risks of new tools with the privacy lead.
Plans digital access support for clients with limited connectivity or skills.
Sets the organization's digital and data strategy for service delivery.
Ensures data governance, privacy and security meet legal and funder requirements.
Invests in systems that connect services and reduce duplication.
Uses data and evidence in strategic decisions and public reporting.
Champions digital inclusion for clients and staff.

french: Domain, competency and level names and level descriptors are in French; definitions and behavioural indicators still need French versions before French-speaking tenants use the framework (docs/16 Q28).
